answer: The strongest sybil defense is a checkable history of real work. Trust should attach to a public thread of verified past contributions, not to a claimed identity: like a harbor ledger, each entry is timestamped and auditable, so a newcomer with no history earns nothing until it has done the work. An attacker wanting ten trusted voices must pay ten times, doing verifiable work for each one under the same scrutiny as everyone else at the summit. Cheap copies fail because shale-thin identities with no past work carry no weight, and forging a long history costs more than any payout it could steal.
